Change c0073. Location: 1818 Vol. I, Ch. II; 1831 Ch. III.

Context before (unchanged): The modern masters promise very little; they know that metals cannot be transmuted, and that the elixir of life is a chimera.

1818 text: But these philosophers, whose hands seem only made to dabble in dirt, and their eyes to pour over the microscope or crucible, have indeed performed miracles. They penetrate into the recesses of nature, and shew how she works in her hiding places. They ascend into the heavens; they have discovered how the blood circulates, and the nature of the air we breathe.

1831 text: But these philosophers, whose hands seem only made to dabble in dirt, and their eyes to pore over the microscope or crucible, have indeed performed miracles. They penetrate into the recesses of nature, and show how she works in her hiding places. They ascend into the heavens: they have discovered how the blood circulates, and the nature of the air we breathe.

Context after (unchanged): They have acquired new and almost unlimited powers; they can command the thunders of heaven, mimic the earthquake, and even mock the invisible world with its own shadows."

result.rationale: Changes are orthographic: 'shew' to 'show' and punctuation swap ';' to ':'. 'pour' to 'pore' is a word-form correction (to pore over) with no shift in meaning, so the edit is largely spelling and punctuation with no interpretive consequence.
